problem: Deep RL and learned planners need large amounts of data, learn reactive policies that do not transfer, and are hard to interpret. Prior differentiable planners (VIN, GPPN) fail to penalise invalid actions such as collisions, and prior option-discovery methods fail to learn options that are both causal and temporally consistent.
motivation: Planning, reasoning and long-horizon decisions in novel scenarios need transferable, interpretable knowledge learned with limited trial and error. This PhD thesis targets spatial reasoning and planning for embodied agents through four contributions: a differentiable planner (CALVIN), unsupervised option discovery (SOAP), LLM code-as-policy optimisation (LangProp), and a staged Minecraft agent (Voggite).
key_idea: Make planning and skills learnable, structured and interpretable: differentiable value iteration with learned action affordance for navigation, options as discrete memory, and LLM-generated code as a policy optimised with IL/RL. The thesis also covers a staged Minecraft agent.
insight: In CALVIN, the ablation on partially observable 2D mazes shows the affordance loss L_A is essential: L_Q+L_A alone gets 8.3% vs 92.2% for the full loss. Without L_P, success is 84.1%. In LangProp, offline IL yields causal confusion (a policy that outputs zero speed when already stopped, scoring 0.0 on test routes), while online IL/RL training fixes it. So the training objective and data distribution decide which code gets selected.
method: CALVIN: differentiable value iteration (Conv2d/Conv3d) on a learned map of embeddings, with learned transition (P), reward (R) and action affordance (A) kernels; trained by imitation with L_Q + L_P + L_A losses, with a reweighted loss. Uses a backbone called LPN for 3D observations.

PPOEM/SOAP: unsupervised option discovery. PPOEM applies forward-backward (Baum-Welch) to option-augmented policies; SOAP extends GAE to propagate option advantages through time, giving a causal option policy conditioned on history only.

LangProp: an LLM (GPT-3.5) generates candidate policy code, which is scored on input-output data. The LLM iteratively updates the best candidates from feedback (exceptions, failed examples), like a training loop with replay buffer, priority and top-N retention.

LangProp CARLA agent: privileged scene info (actors within 50 m, waypoint, traffic light/stop distances) goes to code that outputs a speed category (MOVE/SLOW/STOP) and turning angle, which an external PID controller turns into control. Trained with BC, DAgger, online IL, and IL+RL infraction penalties; infraction samples are weighted 100x.

Voggite: OpenAI VPT backbone with precomputed embeddings and a fine-tuned policy head, plus action-frequency reweighting. A hard-coded 'use' action trigger switches stages. For the waterfall task the agent turns 180° and retreats; for pen/house tasks it lowers move probability and raises use probability.

IIC segmentation (abandoned): invariant information clustering with temporal positive pairs on Minecraft demos; dropped because clusters depend only on the current observation, VPT already provides pretraining, and unimodal clusters are too restrictive.

setting.backbone: CALVIN: LPN (learned mapping) + value-iteration planner, trained from scratch; LangProp: GPT-3.5 (frozen, used as code optimiser); Voggite: OpenAI VPT transformer with fine-tuned policy head
setting.training_data: CALVIN: expert demonstrations in 2D mazes, MiniWorld 3D mazes and AVD; LangProp: CARLA training routes (expert labels + online rollouts); Voggite: 600 h of BASALT expert demonstrations on top of pretrained VPT
setting.observation: CALVIN: partial egocentric observations with depth, known pose and camera parameters; LangProp: privileged CARLA scene state; Voggite: RGB pixels
setting.action_space: CALVIN: discrete grid actions (translation/rotation); LangProp: speed category + angle to PID; Voggite: VPT mouse/keyboard actions
setting.simulator: MiniWorld, CARLA 0.9.10, MineRL/Minecraft, and 2D mazes; AVD is a real-image dataset
setting.privileged: CALVIN assumes known pose, depth and camera parameters; LangProp uses privileged CARLA actor/waypoint/traffic-light info; Voggite uses none

results: CALVIN reaches 92.2% success on partially observable 2D mazes vs 11.25% for GPPN under the reweighted loss, and 69.2% on 8x8 MiniWorld mazes vs 41.2% for VIN. LangProp's online IL/RL agent scores 80.9 on CARLA test routes, above the Roach, TCP, TransFuser and InterFuser experts, but below TF++ (86.1) and its own hand-written expert (95.2). Voggite placed 3rd of 63 in BASALT with average 0.06.
limitations: CALVIN assumes known pose, depth and camera parameters, a static environment, and discrete state/action spaces; trained only with IL.
Voggite's stage triggers and sub-policy changes are hard-coded, with only two options per task; SOAP's options are discrete and sample-inefficient.
LangProp lacks robustness and safety guarantees, and credit assignment for delayed rewards is unresolved; it is evaluated with privileged state, not raw perception.
